answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 72% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned which means nobody profits from it. Because the harbor forfeiture is applied at exit, the pulse ledger totals each burn, and the ember audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 170 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
